To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the spatial alignment effect in pantomimed reaching-to-grasp is modulated by cup distance (near and not near) and that this modulation depends on the actual possibility to grasp the cup”.

(1) the spatial alignment effect influences kinematic parameters of reach-grasp movements only when the cup is reachable; (2) the cup’s location (near and far from body) influences the kinematic parameters of the reach-grasp pantomimes independently of the actual distance from the subject.

1) spatial alignment effect is effective only when the cup is located at near distance; 2) the spatial alignment effect does not depend on the possibility to actually grasp the cup, but only on the distance of the cup from the subject.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the spatial alignment effect is instantiated when the target is located in near and far peripersonal spaces.

the study of the influence of the affordance on the kinematic parameters of reach-to-grasp movements, in a condition where the affordance is not related to the actual possibility of reaching the object.
the role of extrinsic properties of objects (size, distance) in the control of reach-to-grasp movement, in the case of pantomimed movements, which do not require the execution of a movement.

affordance related to spatial alignment effect was effective only if the object was actually reachable.
affordance is instantiated by the actor, and this is influenced by both extrinsic and intrinsic properties of the object, as well as by the possibility to interact with the object.

, during pantomime, the spatial alignment effect is effective only when the object can be reached, and this effect is probably due to a combination of the affordance related to object use and the possibility to reach the object.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of the cup orientation on the kinematic parameters of the pantomime depended on the possibility of actually reaching the cup.
the affordance of an object is instantiated by the observer, but it is not always used to control the action.
the spatial alignment effect is effective only when affordance can be instantiated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial alignment effect is effective only when the object is located within the reachable space.
the affordance related to object use (i.e. the spatial alignment effect) is instantiated even if the target cannot be reached, but only if the object is reachable.
the spatial alignment effect can be observed in near but not far space.
